abstract.para: Reboot a system without waiting for firmware and hardware re-initialization, using &kexec; instead of a normal reboot.

topic.para: The kexec-tools package, which provides &kexec; and the kexec-load.service and kexec.target systemd units, is installed by default. To confirm it is present:

important.title: A &kexec; reboot skips pending boot loader changes
important.para: A &kexec; reboot bypasses firmware and the boot loader entirely. Any boot loader configuration changes you made since the last normal boot are not applied until the computer performs an ordinary hard reboot.

step.para: Make sure no important services are running and no users other than yourself are logged in, since a &kexec; reboot restarts the system immediately once triggered.

systemctl kexec loads the currently running kernel, its initrd, and its kernel command line into memory through kexec-load.service, then immediately hands control to that freshly loaded kernel instead of performing a normal reboot. You do not need to load the kernel manually first.
